role: the reader who holds the spec against itself
verdict: The spec does not yet meet this lens's definition of success: the index lists its pages without binding them, and the largest gap is that the mechanism protecting the merge (a ruleset-required code-owner review) is stated as fact in six places, measured false in one, and caveated rather than deleted, while a release-signing credential is named in one paragraph that no criterion, journey, probe or workflow step consumes.

findings.defect: The code-owner review is stated as the enforcing mechanism in 05 5.3, 05 5.4, 12 12.4, 12 12.9, ADR 0001 rule 8 and ADR 0003 while 10 10.2 item a measures that the default-branch ruleset requires no review, and the spec keeps the stale text with a parenthetical in three cells against ADR 0001 rule 3 (stale content is deleted, not caveated) and 12 12.5 (current state only).
findings.scenario: A contributor reads 12 12.4 or ADR 0001 rule 8, learns that an ADR change needs a code-owner review before it merges, and builds a process on it; a sandbox session merges its own ADR change through the API, which nothing refuses (ADR 0008), and the contributor finds out from the git log.
findings.change: In 05 5.3, 05 5.4 (approval-line row), 12 12.4 (merge row), 12 12.9 (releasable row, agent-and-reviewer paragraph) and 12 12.5, replace every statement that the ruleset requires a review with the measured state: the merge is a working agreement, the approval line is the only recorded approval, and the review is a judgment with no enforcing ruleset until the deferred approval decision is made; keep the one full statement in 05 5.4 and link to it. Mark ADR 0001 rule 8's owner line and ADR 0003's check sentence Superseded by a short new record, since ADR 0001 rule 7 has that status for this case.
findings.cost: About forty words removed and twenty added across five sections; one short ADR that supersedes two sentences of two accepted records; no mechanism.

findings.defect: The Release signing paragraph of 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 decision 6 presuppose an operator-held credential that signs release artifacts, but S1, J1 step 2, 11 11.2 B1 and the release steps of 10 10.2 know only checksums and a provenance attestation, and S1 says the attestation step signed them.
findings.scenario: The sandbox's token pushes a v* tag (ADR 0008); release.yml builds, attests, verifies and publishes; a user runs J1 step 2 and every proof the spec told them to check passes; nothing the operator holds was ever applied to the archives, and the paragraph that said signing is an operator step protected nothing.
findings.change: Decide one of two texts and write it in 10 10.2 Release and bootstrap, S1, J1 step 2 and 11 11.2 B1 together: either a signing step (the artifact, where the operator runs it, the verify command the user runs, and that a local run can produce it, which changes the sentence Build provenance is the one thing a local run cannot produce), or delete the Release signing paragraph and reword ADR 0008 decision 6 to say that no release-signing credential exists and the attestation is the only proof.
findings.cost: A decision by the maintainer; either one mechanism (a signing step, an asset, a verify command, a probe observation) or about sixty words removed in two places.

findings.defect: The word sandbox means two things with one row in 01 1.7: the development sandbox the product is built in (ADR 0008: the operator's account, the forwarded agent holds the signing key and a separate GitHub authentication key) and a romeu-managed sandbox (06 6.4: exactly one signing key, the full host agent never forwarded; 03 3.4), and no page says which one it means.
findings.scenario: A security reviewer reads 06 6.4 and concludes that the agent that builds this product can sign and nothing else; a contributor reads ADR 0008 and concludes that every romeu sandbox forwards the operator's GitHub key; both are wrong about the sandbox they did not read, and the token rows of 05 5.4 are read as the product's security model.
findings.change: Add a row to 01 1.7 for development sandbox (the sbx sandbox this repository is developed in, provisioned outside romeu, with the operator's account and keys) and make the sandbox row say a sandbox romeu created or adopted; in ADR 0008 Context, 05 5.4 (the two token rows and the Verified-signature row) and the deferred rows on the token, write development sandbox where that is what is meant.
findings.cost: One vocabulary row and about a dozen word substitutions; the vocabulary check then catches a bare sandbox on those pages only if the Not column gains nothing, so this stays a review item.

findings.defect: What mise may install is stated four ways that disagree: the 10 10.2 lint row fails any [tools] entry but go, golangci-lint and govulncheck; ADR 0007 rule 8 allows go and golangci-lint only; 12 12.1 and plan.md Toolchain pins put gh in mise.lock and start it through mise exec; ADR 0001 Consequences says a Markdown or spell tool enters pinned through mise.lock like reuse, while 12 12.1 says reuse is a container image because mise cannot pin it.
findings.scenario: The task that lands tools/release verify (T088) adds gh to mise.toml; the lint test of 10 10.2 fails on a tool outside its three; the author loosens the test, types the approval line for the checks surface (05 5.4 says the author types it) and merges, which is the loosening the test existed to refuse; or gh is started through mise exec, the call form 10 10.2 says runs a search-path program with exit 0 when the tool is missing.
findings.change: Write the allowed [tools] set once in 12 12.1 with gh in or out by decision, say in 10 10.2 that the lint test reads that list, make ADR 0007 rule 8 and ADR 0001 Consequences point at it, and decide whether tools/release follows the never through mise exec rule of tools/ci (and say so in 12 12.1).
findings.cost: One decision (gh in mise.lock or installed another way), one list with three pointers, and the lint test reading a list instead of three literals.

findings.defect: Two rules of 03 3.1 read host settings (the repo url host must be a gitHosts entry; the workload repository must be in workloadRepositories) and the same rule table is run by julieta spec validate in the config repo's CI (02 2.2, 04 4.3, 07 7.6, J2 step 1), where no host settings exist, with no sentence saying which validator skips which rule.
findings.scenario: An agent writes projects/foo.yaml with a workload on a registry the host does not allowlist; julieta spec validate passes in CI, the PR merges, and romeu sync exits 2 on the host; the operator reads a green CI and a red host and cannot tell from 03 which rule differs.
findings.change: Add a column or a note to the 03 3.1 table marking the two host-settings rules as romeu-only, and say in the 04 4.3 spec validate row that it reports those two as not checked here (or checks them against a flag that names the allowlists), so one rule table has one written split.
findings.cost: A column and two sentences; rules.go gains a scope attribute per rule, which the generated reference table shows.

findings.defect: julieta pin workload reads a registry and pin check --workflows reads GitHub releases (04 4.3) from inside a sandbox (J9: in the config sandbox), but 07 7.5 derives egress only from locks, the catalog, spec extras and kits, and no catalog list of 03 3.5 names a registry host, so julieta's own network commands have no egress and no page says where they run.
findings.scenario: The agent in the config sandbox runs julieta pin workload projects/foo.yaml as J9 says; the sandbox cannot reach docker.io; the pin is moved by hand on the host, which is the path 00 0.1 says does not exist, or the operator adds a gated egress.extra nobody documented.
findings.change: In 07 7.5 add the egress julieta's own commands need (the registry hosts of workloadRepositories and api.github.com for pin check) as a derived set for the config project, or state in 04 4.3 and J9 that pin workload and pin check run only where the catalog's meta set suffices and name that place.
findings.cost: One derivation step and one catalog decision (registry hosts and their upload flags), or two sentences that narrow where two commands run.

findings.defect: J1 step 5 adds secrets to host settings and nothing else, while 03 3.1 requires gitHosts to hold the repo host and workloadRepositories to hold the workload before a spec validates, 06 6.4 requires signing.agentSocket for a git-ssh-sign project, and no page says whether romeu init seeds any of them.
findings.scenario: A new operator follows J1 as written; romeu sync <cfg> at step 6 exits 2 on the config project's own spec because github.com is not a gitHosts entry or the workload is not allowlisted, and the guide page generated from J1 has no step that explains it.
findings.change: Add a J1 step between 3 and 6 that names the host-settings keys the operator fills (gitHosts, workloadRepositories, signing when used), and say in the 04 4.2 init row and 03 3.4 which keys init writes with defaults and which it leaves for the operator.
findings.cost: One journey step, one sentence in the init row, a defaults column in 03 3.4; the J1 scenario function and commands.yaml gain nothing if init seeds the defaults.

findings.defect: ADR 0007's Threat model defers two escapes (an untracked go.work, a caller GOFLAGS -overlay) until the hook next changes or Q25 is decided, naming a plan deferred-decisions row that plan.md does not have; Q25 is decided in ADR 0008, the index's Deferred decisions holds no row for the two escapes, and nothing reopened them.
findings.scenario: The trigger fired on 2026-10-07 and no table carried the item, so the pre-push hook keeps starting tools/ci in a way both escapes bypass, and the next reader of ADR 0007 finds a pointer to a row that does not exist.
findings.change: Add a row to the index's Deferred decisions (deferred: starting tools/ci from the hook in a way that ignores a parent go.work and the caller's GOFLAGS; until then: the hook as it is; reopened by: the next change to .githooks/ or the token narrowing), and make ADR 0007's paragraph point at that row instead of the plan.
findings.cost: One table row and one sentence; no mechanism until the row fires.

findings.defect: 04 4.1 defines exit 1 as operation failed, and the command tables use 1 for found what you asked me to look for in romeu doctor (any fail), julieta spec validate --catalog (an unknown key or host), julieta lock --check, julieta memory verify, julieta pin check and julieta memory import (invalid > 0), so one code carries two contracts.
findings.scenario: The config repo's validate.yml runs julieta spec validate --catalog; a transient fetch failure and a genuine unknown catalog key both exit 1; a CI script that treats 1 as infrastructure retries the real finding away, or one that treats 1 as a finding files a catalog PR for a network error.
findings.change: Either add a row to the exit-code table of 04 4.1 for a check that found what it looked for (a code the error-id scheme RJ-<exit><nn> can carry) and move the six commands to it, or state in 04 4.1 that 1 covers both and that --json carries the distinction, and give each of the six rows the field that says which.
findings.cost: One exit code and six table cells, or one sentence and six JSON fields; the error-id table and the generated exit-codes page follow.

findings.defect: 04 4.1 says --json exists on every read command; julieta lock --check, memory verify, memory check, handoff show, pin check and spec validate are read commands with no --json in their rows.
findings.scenario: The operator's acceptance file of 10 10.5 wants julieta memory verify per repo as a command item whose stdout sha256 is compared; the text output has no stable form, so the item breaks on a wording change that a JSON document would not have shown.
findings.change: Add --json to the six rows with the schema each emits, or amend 04 4.1 to name the read commands that have no --json and why.
findings.cost: Six flags and six small schemas, or one sentence that narrows the convention.

findings.defect: The romeu approve row says approve <name> makes no sbx call while its Reads cell names live sbx version, J11 step 5 repeats makes no sbx call, and the sync steps call sbx version a read, so either sbx call means mutating sbx call, which 01 1.4 and 01 1.5 never define, or the row contradicts itself.
findings.scenario: An implementer makes approve skip sbx version to honour no sbx call; approve then promotes against a stale toolchain that gate 1 would have refused, and the next run exits 3 after the promotion the operator believed was gated.
findings.change: Define in 04 4.1 Subprocesses that a mutating sbx call is one that changes a sandbox, a policy or a secret and that sbx version and sbx ls --json are reads; then write in the approve row and J11 step 5 makes no mutating sbx call.
findings.cost: One definition and two word substitutions.

findings.defect: 01 1.5 says every command marked P in 04 runs the preflight before any mutating sbx call; romeu sync is not marked P in 04 4.2, runs gate 1 at step 1 and the rest of the preflight at step 9 in prose, and I7's E test lists a sync whose sandbox is running with the P commands, so one mechanism has two markings.
findings.scenario: A reader builds the list of P commands from the 04 4.2 table to write the promotion fault-injection test of 10 10.1 (every P command finishes the promotion or refuses) and leaves sync out, the one command that both promotes and reconciles live egress.
findings.change: Mark sync P in 04 4.2 and say in 01 1.5 that sync runs step 1 before its first sbx read and steps 2 to 6 before its first mutating call (step 9), or rename the mark to say what it means.
findings.cost: One mark and one sentence.

findings.defect: Workspace files are written at each promotion and retire (01 1.2), romeu pull creates review/<dir>/ (04 4.2), boundary D and I13 say review.code-workspace lists review checkouts, and J4 step 4 opens that file right after pull, so a checkout created by pull is listed by no workspace file until the next promotion.
findings.scenario: The operator runs romeu pull on a secondary repo for the first time and opens review.code-workspace as J4 says; the folder is absent; they add it by hand, and the next promotion overwrites their edit, which 01 1.2 says it will.
findings.change: Add review.code-workspace to the Writes cell of the pull row in 04 4.2 and to the writers of the Derived from state row in 01 1.2, or state in J4 and 01 1.2 that the review workspace lists only the checkouts that existed at the last promotion.
findings.cost: Two cells, and pull rewriting one file it already knows how to write.

findings.defect: sandboxOptions (cpus, memory) is stripped from renderDigest and carries no gate tag (01 1.4, 03 3.2) while boundary C says every widening goes through the per-project gate; the exception is listed as today sandboxOptions and never justified, and it is one of two of the 23 except/unless clauses in the spec with no stated reason.
findings.scenario: A spec change moves cpus from 4 to 64 and memory from 8g to 128g; sync promotes without gate 2, status says recreate needed, and the host runs a sandbox sized by an agent's PR with no operator approval, which is the shape boundary C exists to stop.
findings.change: Add one Why for us line to gate 2 in 01 1.4 stating why resource limits are not a widening (or tag them widening if they are), and name the committed list of untagged fields plan.md question 30 proposes so a forgotten tag is a generator failure, not a silent strip.
findings.cost: One sentence and a committed list the generator already needs.

findings.defect: The index principle says every lifecycle is an explicit state machine with a transition table (01 1.6); 01 1.6 holds two tables, the promotion commit is a numbered list with recovery prose, the probe lifecycle is a table in 11 11.4 implemented by tools/ci probes, and 12 12.8 promises four generated diagrams from the 12 12.3 source internal/state transition tables, which hold two.
findings.scenario: The promotion recovery, the one lifecycle whose every missing pair is asserted illegal test cannot exist because it has no table, carries a bug a table would have surfaced; plan.md question 11 asks which reading holds and is unanswered at the candidate tag, when a generator change needs a new candidate (11 11.2).
findings.change: Either give the promotion commit and the probe lifecycle a transition table in internal/state (01 1.6 gains two tables; 11 11.4 points at its table and tools/ci probes reads it), or amend the principle and 12 12.8 to name the two lifecycles that are tables and the two that are not, with a reason.
findings.cost: Two tables and one shared generator, or two sentences and two hand-written diagrams; a decision either way, which plan.md question 11 is waiting for.

findings.defect: 01 1.7 has no row for operator or maintainer, and the two words name the same person in 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 (the operator decided, the maintainer's token) and two roles in 09 (legend [O], the romeu user) and 01 1.1 (host settings operator-owned); and the row for spec (a project's YAML) collides with thirteen self-references on the pages (this spec, the spec already has).
findings.scenario: A guide page written from J1 says the operator; a contributor page written from 12 12.4 says the maintainer; a second adopter (00 0.2) reads both and believes the product has a maintainer role on their host; a reader of 03 3.1 believes spec name is the name of this document.
findings.change: Add rows to 01 1.7 for operator (the person who runs romeu on a host), maintainer (the person who merges in the product repo; today the same person as the operator of the development sandbox), and this specification (never spec on its own); replace the self-references accordingly.
findings.cost: Three rows and about thirteen substitutions; the vocabulary check then fails spec on its own only if the Not column is used, which it should be.

findings.defect: The compatibility check runs before the first call of a session (06 6.3 step 4, 03 3.6) and session is defined nowhere, used in three senses (romeu's session; the agent's session in 08 8.2 and 13 13.2; the autonomous work session of 05 5.4 and the deferred rows); 04 4.2 shows the check in run step 5 only, and stop, salvage and pull also exec julieta.
findings.scenario: An implementer makes run check and stop not; a romeu upgrade replaces .romeu/bin under a running sandbox (01 1.6 step 2 allows it); romeu stop calls a julieta of another protocol without the check, and I30's run-only test is green.
findings.change: Replace first call of a session in 06 6.3 and 03 3.6 with the list of commands that run the check (every command that execs julieta: run, stop, salvage, pull) and add the check to each row's Runs cell in 04 4.2; add a 01 1.7 row for the agent session and use another word for the work session of 05 5.4.
findings.cost: Four table cells and one vocabulary row.

findings.defect: Three stores carry three id and timestamp conventions: ledger event ids are lowercase ULIDs for an APFS case-collision reason (13 13.2, 13 13.3) while memory entry, handoff, candidate, generation and salvage ids are uppercase ULIDs (03 3.8, 03 3.9, 03 3.10) and the memory and handoff file names sit on the same APFS host disk; timestamps are created/updated, observed/ingested and createdAt/closedAt/approvedAt.
findings.scenario: A consumer joins a hook-failed event to the handoff written in the same minute and finds one store lowercase, one uppercase and three timestamp names; the APFS argument of 13 13.3 applies to an agent-writable memory dir too and nobody applied it there.
findings.change: State one ULID case for every file name romeu or julieta writes (lowercase, with the 13 13.3 reason) in 03 3.12 or a new 03 rule, and one pair of timestamp names per role (created by the writer, stamped by romeu) or a sentence that says why each store differs.
findings.cost: One rule and a handful of renamed fields before any code exists.

findings.defect: Q25 is decided and recorded in ADR 0008 and still sits in the Open questions table whose rule says a settled question leaves it, with a Settled by cell in prose (decided; the record leaves this table in T101) that the 10 10.5 check (every probe named in the Settled by column) has no grammar to read.
findings.scenario: tools/ci acceptance parses the Settled by column for probe ids and meets prose; either it skips the row silently or fails on a decided question; a reader counts open questions and counts one that is closed.
findings.change: Remove Q25 from the table now (the ADR exists) and give the Settled by cell a grammar in the paragraph above the table: probe ids, maintainer, or decided: ADR nnnn, which sequences reads.
findings.cost: One row deleted and one sentence; the check gains a three-case grammar.

findings.defect: Several Reopened by cells name a plan step rather than an observable event in use (the start of T005; the PR that lands tools/ci docs; the pull request that adds release.yml; item e), against ADR 0005 decision 3 (the trigger is an event, not a date), and the index and 10 10.2 cite plan task ids (T002, T005, T101) while plan.md says the spec is the plan's source of truth.
findings.scenario: The plan renumbers or merges T005; the trigger points at nothing; sequences passes because three cells are filled; the deferral is reopened by nobody and the approval-recording decision is made by whoever implements pr first.
findings.change: Rewrite each plan-step trigger as the event the step produces (the first pull request that adds a check reading the approval line; the first pull request that adds a Markdown linter), add to 12 12.5 the sentence that the spec names no plan task, and remove the three task ids from the index and 10 10.2.
findings.cost: Five cells reworded and one sentence; no mechanism.

findings.defect: The principle Decide at the last responsible moment and ADR 0005 rule 1 say a merge gate is never deferred; five deferred rows are parts of the merge gate (approval recording and what replaces the code-owner review; required status checks without the bypass; a check that reads the rulesets again; a separate job for the change's tests; the token narrowing), and only the token row records the collision (ADR 0008 Consequences, with the operator's acceptance by name).
findings.scenario: A reviewer applying the principle refuses the next merge-gate deferral while four stand unmarked in the same table, and the table reads as if the principle had one exception when it has five.
findings.change: Add to each of the four rows the words that ADR 0008 gives the fifth (this defers a merge-gate part; the operator accepted the collision on <date>), or move the four under one row that names the collision once and lists its parts.
findings.cost: Four phrases and one acceptance by the maintainer, quoted.

findings.defect: ADR 0005 says open questions and deferrals are two tables because they are two states (a question has a default the spec follows; a deferral is absent until an event), and rows sit in the wrong table by that criterion: the review interval of the token narrowing (until then: every 2 autonomous work sessions) and tuning the ledger's starting values (until then: the proposed defaults) are defaults being followed, and Q23 (a credential added only if a private registry is needed) is absent until an event.
findings.scenario: A contributor looking for what the spec does today about the review interval reads Open questions and finds nothing, because the default lives in the table for things that do not exist yet.
findings.change: Move the two rows to Open questions with a Settled by of maintainer, move Q23 to Deferred decisions with its trigger, and add one sentence under each table heading restating ADR 0005's criterion so the next row lands in the right table.
findings.cost: Three rows moved and two sentences.

findings.defect: When a settled question becomes an ADR is stated three ways: the index (in both cases it becomes an ADR) and 12 12.5 (a settled open question becomes an ADR), ADR 0005 decision 4 (if the decision is expensive to reverse), and 11 11.4's kept row (nothing else to do; the open question is settled).
findings.scenario: A default-kept probe result lands; one implementer writes the ADR the index requires and another closes the question per 11 11.4; tools/ci acceptance later finds a settled question with no record or a record for a trivially reversible default.
findings.change: State the rule once in the index's Open questions paragraph (every settled question becomes an ADR, because the question's existence shows it was worth deciding) and make 11 11.4's kept row and ADR 0005 decision 4 point at it; or adopt ADR 0005's narrower rule everywhere.
findings.cost: One decision between two existing sentences and two pointers.

findings.defect: The telemetry row says romeu starts sbx with a fixed environment and sets one variable in a sandbox, JULIETA_MANIFEST (04 4.1, I1), citing I1 for a claim it does not make (I1 is about panes and the final argv), while 04 4.1 adds SSH_AUTH_SOCK to the sbx environment for a git-ssh-sign project and Q19 forwards that socket into the sandbox.
findings.scenario: A reader strengthens the citation into an invariant (romeu passes exactly one variable) and writes a test that fails the day a git-ssh-sign project syncs.
findings.change: Cite 04 4.1 Subprocesses alone and write the claim as it stands there: a scrubbed environment for the sbx process, with SSH_AUTH_SOCK for one kit, and JULIETA_MANIFEST as the only --env romeu passes into a sandbox.
findings.cost: One cell reworded.

findings.defect: The opening of 03 says every format has a version field, strict decoding, a JSON Schema in schemas/ and examples validated in CI, and ledger-entry/v1 and ledger-view/v<n> (13 13.7: only runtime-event has a schema), dora.v1 (12 12.10), e2e/scenarios/commands.yaml (ADR 0001 rule 13) and the pin file (plan.md T012) have none, nor a row in 02 2.1's schema list.
findings.scenario: tools/ci schema passes because it checks only the schemas that exist; a change to the view files' shape is caught by a golden but by no schema, and the sentence every format stays a universal with no measurement.
findings.change: Either add the missing schemas to 02 2.1 and to 13 13.7 and 12 12.10, or weaken the 03 opening to name the formats that have a schema and say why the others do not (a file read by one program and pinned by a golden).
findings.cost: Five schema files and three sentences, or one sentence that drops a universal.

findings.defect: The merge-commit rule has two incompatible reasons: 12 12.9 and ADR 0002 Consequences say a pull request's commits reach main as written, which is what the fix marker and the release notes read; 12 12.10 Inputs and ADR 0004 decision 3 read a change's commits from the GitHub API per pull request so the result does not depend on how a merge was made.
findings.scenario: A reviewer asked why squash is off cites ADR 0002; another cites ADR 0004 to say it would not matter; the setting survives on a reason one record says is not a reason.
findings.change: Keep one reason in 12 12.9 (the one ADR 0004 and 12 12.10 support, or the one about main's history being the commits as written) and make the other record's sentence point at it; ADR 0001 rule 11's aside that a squash merge can make the title a subject goes with it.
findings.cost: Two sentences aligned; no mechanism.

findings.defect: Not in v1 has four homes with three shapes: non-goals (00 0.3), the v1.1 row of 00 0.5, the publishing path designed with its own trigger in 06 6.6 (mandatory when the product is promoted for public use) and the run-layout renderer interface built for tmux and cmux (00 0.3), and the Deferred decisions table; the principle says a mechanism the start does not need gets one row in that table, and 06 6.6 also names a host-settings key (kits.source: published) absent from 03 3.4.
findings.scenario: A contributor asks whether kits may be published yet; the answer is in 06 6.6's Trigger cell, which sequences never reads and which no review round re-reads with the deferred table.
findings.change: Move the 06 6.6 trigger and the renderer-interface item into Deferred decisions as rows (until then: local kits; one renderer), keep 06 6.6 as the design they point at, and say in 00 0.3 that a non-goal has no trigger while a deferral has one.
findings.cost: Two rows and two pointers.

findings.defect: 00 0.5 says every v1 feature traces to a criterion, an invariant, a journey or a maintainer's need, and its table omits the ledger commands (romeu ledger ingest, ledger query, julieta event add, event list), romeu pull, romeu retire, julieta lock, julieta spec validate and julieta pin workload, so the universal is unmeasured.
findings.scenario: The scope skeptic asks what romeu ledger query is for; the only answer is in 13 13.9, and 00 0.5's claim that every feature is traced cannot be checked because the table is a sample.
findings.change: Either complete the table from the command rows of 04 4.2 and 04 4.3 (one row per command, Needed by filled), or reword the opening to say the table lists the features whose need was questioned in review.
findings.cost: About ten rows, each one citation, or one sentence.

findings.defect: 13 13.5 says a project created later under a retired project's name reads those entries as its own because the name is the identity; I33 promises a sandbox reads its own project's entries and, of other projects, closed fields only; the retired project's ids and full events reach the new project's own.jsonl, and no 05 5.4 row and no deferred row carries it.
findings.scenario: An operator retires shop, later creates a different shop for another client; the new sandbox's julieta event list and SessionStart show the earlier project's failure history with its ids, which 13 13.2 says do not cross projects.
findings.change: Add a row to 05 5.4 (why accepted: the name is the identity in v1; mitigation: retire prints the count of entries the name holds) and a sentence in I33 that own means entries ingested under this name, including a retired project's; or add a deferred row for a project identity other than the name with its trigger (the first reuse of a retired name).
findings.cost: One risk row and one clause, or one deferred row.

findings.defect: The memory layout allowlist (08 8.1, I24) admits import/ and nothing describes what it holds, who writes it or which caps apply; julieta memory import reads a <file> argument (03 3.9), and the string import/ occurs in the corpus only in those two rows.
findings.scenario: An agent writes anything it likes under memory/<dir>/import/; the allowlist admits the directory, the per-file caps are stated for entries and handoffs only, and the salvage cap bounds snapshot and salvage payloads, so the one directory with no stated purpose is the one with no stated bound.
findings.change: Either describe import/ in 08 8.1 (content: the JSONL files memory import reads and keeps; writer: julieta; cap) and in 03 3.9, or remove it from both allowlists.

postmortem: v1.0.0 has failed, as this reader saw it fail. (1) The merge gate was a sentence: four pages and two ADRs said the ruleset required a code-owner review (05 5.3, 05 5.4, 12 12.4, 12 12.9, ADR 0001 rule 8, ADR 0003); the measurement said no (10 10.2 item a) and the fix was a parenthetical in three cells, not the deletion ADR 0001 rule 3 requires; the first session that merged its own branch broke nothing it had read; quietly, we chose not to rewrite two ADRs we liked (ADR 0008). (2) Nobody signed the release and everyone thought someone had: 05 5.4 and ADR 0008 decision 6 named an operator-held signing credential; S1, J1 step 2, B1 and release.yml (10 10.2) knew only checksums and an attestation, and S1 said the attestation signed them. (3) sync exited 2 on day one: J1 step 5 filled secrets only; 03 3.1 needed gitHosts and workloadRepositories first; in the config repo's CI the same rules ran without host settings (02 2.2, 04 4.3, J2 step 1), so CI was green while the host refused. (4) The agent could not move the pin from where we told it to: julieta pin workload (04 4.3, J9) read a registry from a sandbox whose egress came from locks, catalog and kits (07 7.5), and no registry host was anywhere; the pin moved by hand on the host, the path 00 0.1 promised did not exist. (5) Four lists of what mise may install, and the release tool broke the strictest: 10 10.2's lint test allowed three tools, ADR 0007 rule 8 two, 12 12.1 added gh behind mise exec, the call 10 10.2 said runs a stray program on a missing tool; T088 loosened the test and the approval line was typed by its author (05 5.4); quietly, the lint row is 900 words and nobody reads 900 words twice. (6) Two sandboxes, one word: in ADR 0008 and the token rows of 05 5.4 the sandbox was the one we built in (operator account, two keys forwarded, admin everywhere); in 06 6.4 it was a romeu-managed one (one signing key, never the full agent); readers of each believed the other's rules held for them; 01 1.7 defines sandbox once and we never asked which one a page meant. (7) The lifecycle rule covered the two machines that had tables (index, 01 1.6); the promotion commit stayed prose, the probe lifecycle lived in tools/ci probes (11 11.4), 12 12.8 promised four diagrams from two tables; the bug was in promotion recovery, the lifecycle whose every-missing-pair test could not exist (plan question 11, never answered). (8) Deferred decisions scheduled; they did not defer: triggers like the start of T005 were plan steps, sequences checked that three cells were filled and not that one named an event; ADR 0007's two go run escapes waited until Q25 was decided, Q25 was decided and no row existed to reopen them; five deferrals crossed a merge gate is never deferred (ADR 0005 rule 1) and one recorded the crossing. (9) A ledger identity was a name, and names come back: 13 13.5 let a project under a retired name read the old project's entries, ids included, as its own; I33 promised its own project's entries; 05 5.4 listed six ledger risks and not this one. (10) The vocabulary policed the words nobody used: tools/ci vocabulary fails the Not column (01 1.7); sandbox probe was defined and used once, sandbox-side check seven times; session had three senses and no row and decided when the compatibility check ran (06 6.3); a check that cannot fail on the defined word proves only that the table exists. (11) The index listed; it did not bind: stated once was stated five times; open questions lived in two tables (index; plan questions 3 to 13); not in v1 had four homes (00 0.3, 00 0.5, 06 6.6, Deferred decisions); three rules said when a settled question becomes an ADR (index, 11 11.4, ADR 0005); two ADRs gave opposite reasons for merge commits (ADR 0002 vs ADR 0004; 12 12.9 vs 12 12.10); no product bug, but each a fork where the next contributor picked one reading and sandboxes picked differently; quietly, eight rounds added text and none removed a second copy.
lens_critique: This lens equates success with one mechanism and one name, and this product's security model wants the opposite in places: the forbidden-name check runs in the hook, in hygiene and in pr on purpose; CODEOWNERS is generated and also an ask-first path as defence in depth (12 12.3); gate 1, gate 2 and sbx's own prompt overlap by design (01 1.4). Counted by this lens those are three findings; counted by the product they are layers, and the lens cannot tell a redundant copy from an independent check without the threat model it does not read. The lens also rewards agreement over truth: the code-owner review was stated consistently in six places and was false in all six, which this lens only notices because one place disagreed; a spec that had deleted the measurement would have passed this lens better and protected the merge worse. And success for this product is a developer losing no work and a host not falling (00 0.1), which no cross-reading measures; the lens finds forks in the text, and most forks it finds cost a sentence to close, so its findings are many and its Blocking ones few, and a reader should weigh its count accordingly.
missing_viewpoint: The implementing agent that reads one section cold: the spec scores pages on AI retrievability (ADR 0001 rule 18) and expects agents to build from it (00 0.2, 12 12.2), yet no lens is the reader who is handed 04 4.3 or 13 13.4 alone, without the index, and must act on it; L3 reads whole, L5 uses the product, L8 maintains generated docs, and none of them is the one-section reader whose misreadings are the defects the plan's 102 tasks will actually produce.
